docRequirement: claude-directory.md makes per-subagent memory part of the documented directory LAYOUT, in three places. (a) The project tree node at :376-402: `agent-memory/` with `autogen: true` and `badge: 'committed'`, oneLiner "Subagent persistent memory, separate from your main session auto memory", `when: 'First 200 lines (capped at 25KB) of MEMORY.md loaded into the subagent system prompt when it runs'`, children `<agent-name>/` -> `MEMORY.md` (also `autogen: true`, "Loaded into the subagent system prompt when the subagent starts", "the subagent creates and updates this file itself. You do not write it"). Its tips fix the scope->path mapping and the version-control split: "Only created for subagents that set the `memory:` frontmatter field"; `memory: project` is "meant to be shared with your team", `memory: local` "writes to `.claude/agent-memory-local/` instead" to keep memory out of version control, `memory: user` "writes to `~/.claude/agent-memory/`". (b) The Global tree node at :690-698: `~/.claude/agent-memory/`, `autogen: true`, same load-at-start `when`. (c) The summary table at :1503: `agent-memory/<name>/` | Project and global | Commit ✓ | "Persistent memory for subagents". So the binding is: the runtime CREATES these directories on demand for an agent that declares `memory:`, the subagent reads and writes `MEMORY.md` inside its own `<agent-name>/` subdirectory, and the first 200 lines / 25KB of that file are injected into the subagent's system prompt at spawn.

Add the two directory names — `export const AGENT_MEMORY_DIR = 'agent-memory'`, `export const AGENT_MEMORY_LOCAL_DIR = 'agent-memory-local'` — and one resolver, `agentMemoryDirPath(scope: AgentMemoryScope, agentName: string, opts: { projectRoot?: string; configDir?: string }): string`, mapping the page's three rows onto Nessy paths: `user` -> join(configDir ?? CONFIG_DIR, 'agent-memory', name) (CONFIG_DIR = ~/.nessy-agent, packages/shared/src/config/paths.ts:18-21); `project` -> join(projectRoot, NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR, 'agent-memory', name); `local` -> join(projectRoot, NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR, 'agent-memory-local', name). MUST sanitize `agentName` to a single path segment — imported Claude/Codex plugin agent keys carry ':' and '/' (they arrive through runtime-agent-definition.ts:616-620) — and MUST refuse a symlinked namespace the way cron-store.ts:124 already does (`assertNotSymlink(join(projectDir, NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR), …)`); reuse that helper rather than inventing a second containment rule.

Add `export const MEMORY_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024` — it does not exist today — and give `readMemoryFile` (:29-33) an optional byte cap so it stops at whichever of 200 lines / 25KB comes first. Add `loadAgentMemoryPromptBlock(scope, agentName, opts)`: returns '' when `getMemoryEnabled()` is false (storage.ts:1104-1111, same gate `isMemoryEnabled` applies at :144/:322), else mkdir -p the resolved directory and return a block that names the absolute directory, instructs read+write, inlines the capped `MEMORY.md`, and adds a curate-if-truncated instruction only when a cap actually truncated. Do NOT route this through `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (:317-334): that one merges and dedups the session/user/project tier through `seenMemoryFiles`, and folding per-agent memory in would cross-contaminate the main session's block.

claude-directory.md marks `agent-memory/` committed and `agent-memory-local/` the keep-it-out-of-git alternative. The fork has no mechanism for that half: nothing writes a project `.gitignore` (verified — no writer exists). Cheapest faithful implementation is to write a one-line `.gitignore` containing `*` inside `agent-memory-local/` when that directory is first created; do not touch the repository's own root `.gitignore` (which already ignores `.nessy-agent/` wholesale at .gitignore:61 — a repo-local dev convenience, not a shipped template, and it would also hide the committed project scope from a real user's team).

One line: drop "the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet provisioned — see the R30c report" and cite claude-directory.md:376-402 / sub-agents.md#enable-persistent-memory instead. Also update the path list at :40-41 to the Nessy paths actually created.

Readers of that object: spawner.ts:552-581 (producer), SessionManager.ts:10873-11133 (host validator/recomposer, which clamps tools, maxTurns, permissionMode and worktreePolicy from the same literal), packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:571 (shape validation). Tool-list widening reaches the child's permission gate through `inheritedTools` (SessionManager.ts:10993-10995) and the skill `disallowedTools` chokepoint (:11011-11018). Worktree interaction is the sharp edge: SessionManager.ts:10400-10405 swaps the project handle for a worktree lease path when `worktreePolicy === 'isolated-worktree'`, and the fork has no `.worktreeinclude` support at all (verified: zero hits repo-wide), so nothing copies gitignored memory into a worktree — the directory must be resolved from the parent's project root instead. New filesystem surface under `<project>/.nessy-agent/` and `<configDir>/`: outside the containment set native-sources.ts scans (:1013-1043), so per-agent files will not leak into the session capability view — confirm that stays intended. Definition-side carriers already holding the field and unaffected by shape: definitions.ts:454/:702, runtime-agent-definition.ts:371/:661, runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173. Imported-plugin path: plugin-supplied agent names contain ':' and '/' and would become directory names, so sanitization is a security requirement, not cosmetics.
userImpact: Observable today, silently. Declare `memory: project` (or `user`/`local`) on an agent — in `orchestratorAgents` in config.json, in `.nessy-agent/agents/<name>.md` frontmatter, or by importing a Claude plugin agent that uses the field — and it validates, round-trips and then behaves exactly as if the field were absent. Follow the documented directory layout afterwards and there is nothing to find: no `.nessy-agent/agent-memory/<name>/`, no `.nessy-agent/agent-memory-local/`, no `~/.nessy-agent/agent-memory/`, no `MEMORY.md`, and no warning, log line or UI affordance saying per-agent memory is unsupported. Run the agent twice and the second run has learned nothing. The sharpest case is the one the docs' own example produces: a `code-reviewer` with `toolset: read-only` told in its body to update its agent memory gets tools `['read','grep','find','ls']`, so it either skips the instruction or burns a turn on a tool it does not have. Users importing Claude subagent bundles hit this without ever writing the field themselves.
